doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Songwriting and her first published lyric for Ivan Lins
summary: She writes few songs but wrote lyrics for an Ivan Lins love song that they recorded as a duet.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. Do you have aspirations to write original material?

I’m not really much for songwriting. I used to do tons of it. The way I look at it there are just way too many great songs that I’d want to sing and I couldn’t get through them in a lifetime so when am I going to find time to sing something I wrote that’s not as good. But I do love to write lyrics. I do. Occasionally I’ve been given tunes by people to write lyrics to. And actually my first published lyric has just happened. And it’s really like the proudest moment of my entire career because it’s for one of Ivan Lins tune.

It’s for an Ivan Lins tune. And I idolize him. His music means everything to me. I sing so many of his tunes. I’ve recorded four duets with him. Actually the fourth duet is the song. He sent me the song to write the lyrics to and then we recorded this duet for this album. I’m not sure if it’s out yet. I don’t know what the album is called. I don’t know if it’s going to be released in the States.
It’s his album. It’s a big duets album with orchestra. It’s like a huge project. But yeah, I’m just beyond excited about it. I can’t believe it even happened.
Did he give you any guidance with what he was looking for with the song? Did the song have a title?

No it didn’t yet. But he told me. It’s a love song. Ivan writes love songs. He either writes love songs or political statements. You know in the great Brazilian tradition. You know a lot of great Brazilian music is very politically minded. I mean you look at a lot of these lyrics and they’re, you know — but yeah, it’s also the great love songs, and that’s what this was.
